no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

response: {"headline": "The ACCELERATE trial of evacetrapib was stopped for futility in 12,092 high-risk vascular patients, confirming that CETP inhibition does not reduce cardiovascular events despite massive HDL-C elevation.", "summary": "The ACCELERATE trial randomized 12,092 patients with high-risk vascular disease to evacetrapib 130 mg or placebo, with a primary composite endpoint of CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina. The trial was stopped early by an independent DSMB on October 12, 2015, for insufficient efficacy after a median follow-up of 1.5 years and 1,670 planned events. Evacetrapib achieved its intended pharmacodynamic effect, raising HDL-C by 129% (non-placebo-adjusted) and 103% (placebo-adjusted) in phase 2, but Mendelian randomization and prior CETP inhibitor failures established that HDL-C elevation is not causal for CVD risk reduction. The modest placebo-adjusted LDL-C lowering of 15% (0.56 mmol/L) yielded an expected hazard ratio of 0.943 with only 22% power, making the trial underpowered even if LDL-C lowering were the sole mechanism.
